subject: Re: ACME - Latency & SLA follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@acme.com>, Olivia Park <olivia.park@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: ACME discovery - performance / SLO recap and next steps

Hi Jordan / Olivia,

Thanks again for taking the time today - great conversation. Quick recap of the performance points we covered and proposed next steps so we're aligned: 

Summary of ACME targets
- Target latency: P95 end-to-end generation <= 200 ms for short interactive prompts (avg prompt length ~30 tokens).
- P99 target: <= 500 ms (nice-to-have, limited scope).
- Throughput: target baseline 250 req/s sustained per region, peak burst to 500 req/s.
- Concurrency: typical concurrent sessions ~350, peak expected 700.
- Streaming: token-streaming to client required for interactive UI (we'll provide examples of chunking expectations).

How we measure latency (proposal)
- Redwood measures latency server-side: time from receipt of request by our ingress to the first token output (for streaming) and to final token for non-streaming.
- Proposal for SLA: P95 measured on server-side end-to-end processing time for requests that are not excluded (see exclusions below).

Exclusions and considerations
- Warm-up / cold-start windows after deploys (15 minutes per instances during rollouts)
- Customer-triggered heavy-preprocessing (if ACME pipeline does large pre-processing outside Redwood)
- Force majeure / planned maintenance windows with 72-hour prior notice

Reporting cadence and remedies
- Weekly perf dashboard with token/latency breakdowns and daily SLO snapshots.
- SLA remedies: service credits tiered by monthly availability/latency failures (we will propose language for legal).

Next steps (action items)
1) Marissa / Aditya: share perf test harness and sample payloads (I attached a draft perf harness + initial SLA language).
2) ACME: share representative traffic traces or sample payloads (Olivia/Jordan).
3) Redwood infra: run a controlled benchmark with ACME samples and report P95/P99, throughput at target concurrency.
4) Legal sync: exchange draft SLA language and iterate (I included an initial draft for review).

I attached a short draft SLA and the perf harness (zip) to get us started. If that looks good I'll schedule a 30-min follow-up next week to walk through results and tweak targets.

Thanks,

--
Marissa Cole

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@acme.com>

Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 09:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME discovery - performance / SLO recap and next steps

Thanks Marissa - helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side so the benchmarking is aligned: 

1) Latency measurement: for our use case the client-perceived first-byte time is what matters (time from when user clicks to first token visible in UI). If Redwood measures ingress-to-first-token, can you confirm network hops on our side are minimal? We'll share trace examples.

2) Streaming behavior: we typically send short prompts and expect first token within ~120-150 ms under normal load. Subsequent tokens can stream at ~20-30 ms/token. Can Redwood's runtime guarantee the initial decoding latency separately from per-token throughput?

3) Exclusions: are you amenable to excluding start-of-day cold starts and any scheduled maintenance that is longer than 10 minutes (we can accept planned windows but want visibility)?

4) Remedies: for the first pass, can you outline the credit structure you envision for latency SLO misses (P95 breaches)? ACME legal will want a clear waterfall to evaluate exposure.

We'll package and send a set of sample payloads and a 48-hour trace dump by EOD Friday.

-Jordan
Product Lead, ACME
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@acme.com>, Olivia Park <olivia.park@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 11:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME discovery - performance / SLO recap and next steps

Jordan - thanks, great questions. Answers inline below.

1) Client-perceived first-byte vs server-side measurement
- Our measurement: server-side ingress-to-first-token is the canonical measurement for Redwood SLAs (removes variability from customer network).
- Pragmatically we'll correlate with client-side first-byte during benchmarking. If network adds >30 ms median variance we'll note that and scope a joint optimization.

2) Streaming guarantees
- The runtime differentiates initial decode latency vs steady-state token emit rates. For interactive short prompts we can target initial P95 <= 150 ms in our Dedicated offering with pinned capacity; hosted tier generally targets P95 <= 200-250 ms depending on model/quant.
- Per-token steady-state: expect 15-240 ms/token depending on model size and CPU/GPU mode; we'll provide model-specific profiles.

3) Exclusions
- We can accept excluding scheduled maintenance windows > 10 minutes if ACME is given 48 hours notice for planned maintenance.
- Warm-up windows of 15 minutes per rollout are reasonable; we'll document this in SLA.

4) Remedies / Credit structure (initial proposal)
- Tiered credits based on monthly % of requests meeting P95:
  - >=99.9%: no credits
  - 99.0-99.9%: 10% monthly service credit
  - 97.0-99.0%: 25% monthly service credit
  - <97.0%: 50% monthly service credit + joint remediation review
- We'll treat latency SLOs separately from availability metrics in the contract. Legal can iterate on exact thresholds.

Attachments: I've uploaded a short draft SLA (redwood-acme-draft-sla-v1.pdf) and a small perf harness with runner scripts (acme-perf-harness.zip). Please confirm you can open the zip and we'll schedule a run next week.

Next step: Aditya / Vivek will run an initial run using ACME traces once you send them, and we'll book a 30-min follow-up next week (suggest Tue 12/1 10am PT).

Best,

--
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Looping back - we ran a brief dry-run with the sample prompts Marissa shared internally (no ACME trace yet). Quick notes: 

- On our Dedicated config (pinned node pool, A100 class), measured server-side ingress-to-first-token P95 ~ 140 ms for the short prompts (30 tokens). P99 ~ 340 ms.
- Sustained throughput: 275 req/s at steady-state with 350 concurrent sessions; we saw GPU saturation at ~480 req/s.
- Streaming: initial token latency looks good; per-token steady-state ~22 ms/token for the model variant used.

Action items:
- Marissa: confirm Tue 12/1 10am PT follow-up with ACME (Jordan) and we'll run the ACME trace this afternoon.
- Vivek: create a short perf-report (P95/P99 histograms + CPU/GPU metrics) and drop into the Drive link.

If ACME's traces show higher network-induced first-byte variance we'll note client-side network in the report and suggest steps (CDN near edge, keepalive tuning).

- Aditya
